segments.name: AI cloud infrastructure
segments.note: Renting out GPU-powered cloud capacity purpose-built for AI training and inference (running trained models); the company's single revenue line, up 112% YoY as demand from AI labs, hyperscalers and enterprises surged.

opex.name: Technology and infrastructure
opex.note: Running and expanding the platform: data-center operations and the engineering behind the AI cloud; up from $670M a year ago as capacity grew.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Selling the cloud to AI labs, hyperscalers and large enterprises.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office: finance, legal and company-wide administration.

oneTimers: Other income included an unrealized investment gain: the non-GAAP reconciliation removes $109M of 'other adjustments' — described as primarily a net unrealized gain on investments — on the way from the GAAP net loss of $626M to the adjusted net loss of $567M.
verdict: CoreWeave's revenue more than doubled to $2.6B on AI demand and its backlog reached $104B, but $640M of net interest turned a near-breakeven operating result into a $626M net loss.
otherDetail: Net non-operating expense of $515M: interest expense, net was $640M — the cost of borrowing heavily to build data centers — partly offset by $125M of other income, net. There was no fair-value gain or loss this quarter.
footerNote: CoreWeave's release does not print a gross-profit line; gross profit here is revenue less cost of revenue, exactly as its statement of operations foots. Chart note: CoreWeave's running costs alone exceeded its gross profit, and net interest and other non-operating costs added $515M more, so the chart draws the $626M net loss as a 'Covered by cash on hand' source that funds the operating gap, the interest and the $62M tax bill — the shortfall came from the balance sheet, not from revenue.

kpis.note: diluted net loss per share, vs -$0.60 a year ago

kpis.label: Revenue backlog
kpis.note: at Jun 30, 2026, plus $25B+ added in early Q3

kpis.label: Capex
kpis.note: purchases of property and equipment in Q2 alone

follow100Note: The striking thing: interest and other non-operating costs took $20 of every $100 — almost as much as the $24.31 lost overall. The business was nearly breakeven before the cost of its debt.

takeaways.title: Revenue more than doubled
takeaways.text: Revenue hit $2,575M, up from $1,212M a year ago, and the revenue backlog — work customers have committed to — reached about $104B at quarter-end, with over $25B more added in early Q3.

takeaways.title: Interest is what makes it a loss
takeaways.text: Operations lost only $49M, but net interest expense was $640M. After $125M of other income and $62M of tax, the net loss was $626M — the price of borrowing to build ahead of demand.

takeaways.title: Spending to build is enormous
takeaways.text: CoreWeave spent $6,422M on property and equipment in the quarter — about 2.5 times its revenue — while operating cash flow was $679M. Active power grew by nearly 500 MW to 1.5 GW, with about 3.7 GW contracted.
